results.summary_before: Wildcat is an educational three-stage RISC-V core written in Chisel, taped out with a minimal assembler program that counts up and displays the value on a 7-segment display. It exposes eight input pins, eight bidirectional pins and eight output pins, and requires no external hardware beyond the demo board display. Testing consists of letting it run and observing the 7-segment display counting from 0 to F. A silicon test report confirms the counting works, though the tester's PMOD was active low so the segments appeared inverted.
